rules.title: 2026 rent control ballot initiative (struck by SJC)
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide ballot question to limit annual rent increases was blocked by the Supreme Judicial Court and will not appear on the November 2026 ballot because its religious-use exemption violates the state Constitution's limits on initiative subjects. No rent cap took effect.
rules.citation: MA 2026 rent control ballot initiative petition (SJC decision, June 2026)
rules.quoted_span: The proposal limits annual rent increases for residences, but it carved out exemptions for several types of units, including ones “operated solely for … religious … purposes."
rules.key_value: Annual rent increase cap proposal; struck from 2026 ballot
rules.exemptions: Proposal exempted several unit types, including units operated solely for religious purposes
rules.conflict_note: Petition number not given in the document. Supporters hinted at a 2028 refiling.

no_rule_findings.finding: The proposed rent control ballot question was struck by the SJC in June 2026, so no new rent cap exists as of the query date. The document does not cite the existing state bar on rent control (G.L. c.40P).
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.

parsed.doc_summary: WBUR, June 23, 2026: the Massachusetts SJC struck the statewide rent control ballot initiative from the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-use exemption. A compromise bill was not passed before July 1. Supporters may try again in 2028.
